pattern.top_pattern: CA HMO acute hospital spend is highly concentrated at UCI MEDICAL CENTER
pattern.what_is_impacting: CA Commercial Local Group / HMO / ACUTE HOSPITAL
key_driver_codes: Degenerative Nervous System Disorders without MCC
pattern.pattern_details: CA HMO acute hospital cost growth is dominated by UCI MEDICAL CENTER. The increase reflects both higher use and higher cost per case, which makes this a provider concentration issue rather than a broad statewide trend. A small number of very expensive neurological cases also contributed, but the main business lever is concentrated provider economics at one hospital.
pattern.why_it_matters: This is the largest single cost signal and it is concentrated enough to support targeted network, reimbursement, and utilization action.
pattern.recommended_next_step: Open a joint UCI MEDICAL CENTER review covering contract terms, admission and level-of-care management, and steerage options for CA HMO members.
evidence_summary: UCI MEDICAL CENTER accounts for about $5.2M of the $5.4M increase.
Claim count rose by 247 and paid per admit increased by about $19.7K in CA HMO acute hospital business.
A very small number of degenerative nervous system disorder cases added about $226K, showing high-cost episode risk on top of the provider concentration.
